finding: LibreCAD and ezdxf use polyline paths for MPOLYGON. The upstream writer retained a closed LINE/ARC path as edges, so LibreCAD's polyline readback expectation failed.
change: Project connected closed LINE/ARC edge loops to closed bulge polylines using the DXF clockwise angle convention. Keep other paths in the pre-existing edge form. Retain boundary handles and do not mutate the source object.
verification: The generated control fails on the prior library for all eight closed semicircle profiles and passes after the change.

A 64-profile matrix covers clockwise/counterclockwise quarter, half, major and wrapped arcs; connected and gapped loops; ASCII/Binary; AC1021/AC1032; invalid-radius refusal with sentinel preservation and same-writer corrected retry; source object state; and typed geometry/handle readback.

Independent ezdxf 1.4.5 reconstructs center, radius, endpoints, sweep and direction for all 16 connected generated profiles (four arc sweeps, clockwise/counterclockwise, ASCII/Binary); the optional peer tool generates and removes its own scratch DXFs.
The selected HATCH boundary, MPOLYGON default, and seven-revision HATCH/MPOLYGON allocation transaction tests pass.
The upstream-linked LibreCAD combined selector improves from 10/12 to 11/12 cases passing (155/163 assertions).
limits: Endpoint continuity uses 64 machine epsilons times coordinate scale, so the conversion can normalize gaps within that numeric tolerance; larger gaps retain their original edge form.
Full-circle arcs, single-edge loops, splines, ellipses and other unsupported projections retain the prior output path; no curve flattening or broader native interoperability is claimed.

The remaining consumer test expects rejection for several nonprojected edge profiles; reconcile this with upstream's existing representation and source-preservation requirements before changing the behavior.
No DWG or DXF fixture files were added.
